title: Quasi-compact opens of a Galois base change are defined over a finite subextension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $\bar k/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] that is Galois, i.e. separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (for every $\alpha\in\bar k$ the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $\bar k[T]$); it may be of infinite degree. Write $\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ for the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $\bar k$. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] and $X_{\bar k}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ its base change [def-pc-base-change]. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ let $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):X_{\bar k}\to X_{\bar k}$ be the base change of the $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; it is an automorphism of the scheme $X_{\bar k}$, and $(\sigma\circ\tau)_X=\tau_X\circ\sigma_X$. Let $V\subseteq X_{\bar k}$ be a quasi-compact open subset. Then: (1) there are a subfield $k'$ with $k\subseteq k'\subseteq\bar k$ and $\dim_kk'<\infty$, and a quasi-compact open subset $V'\subseteq X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$, such that $V=p^{-1}(V')$, where $p:X_{\bar k}\to X_{k'}$ is the morphism $\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(k'\hookrightarrow\bar k)$; (2) for this $k'$, $\sigma_X(V)=V$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ that fixes $k'$ pointwise. (Stacks states (2) as: $V$ is invariant under an open subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(\bar k/k)$; the subgroup fixing a finite subextension is such a subgroup.)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 04KU (lemma-Galois-action-quasi-compact-open, lines 876--897), whose proof uses Lemma Tag 0388 (lemma-descend-open, lines 811--848); the action is equation (equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar), lines 850--874

proof.text: The automorphisms $\sigma_X$. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$, $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ is a morphism of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ because $\sigma$ is a $k$-algebra map, and by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)=\operatorname{Spec}(\tau\circ\sigma)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. The base change $g\mapsto g_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}g$ [def-pc-base-change] is functorial ($ (g\circ h)_X=g_X\circ h_X$, $(\mathrm{id})_X=\mathrm{id}$, by the uniqueness in the universal property of the fibre product). Hence $(\sigma\circ\tau)_X=\tau_X\circ\sigma_X$, and $\sigma_X$ is an automorphism of $X_{\bar k}$ with inverse $(\sigma^{-1})_X$; in particular $\sigma_X$ is a bijection of the underlying set.

source.place: Varieties, text before Lemma Tag 04KU, lines 850--874 (equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar)

proof.text: Descent to a finitely generated subalgebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-qc-open-fg-subalgebra] to $X$ and the $k$-algebra $A=\bar k$: there are a $k$-subalgebra $A'\subseteq\bar k$, finitely generated as a $k$-algebra, say by $a_1,\dots,a_n$, and a quasi-compact open $V'\subseteq X_{A'}$ with $V=\pi^{-1}(V')$, where $\pi=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(A'\hookrightarrow\bar k)$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 04KU, proof, line 893 (By Lemma 0388 ...), with Lemma Tag 0388 (lemma-descend-open, lines 811--821)

proof.text: $A'$ is a finite subextension; proof of (1). Since $\bar k/k$ is Galois it is algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], so each $a_i$ is a root of a nonzero $P_i\in k[T]$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]; dividing $P_i$ by its leading coefficient (a unit of the field $k$) gives a monic polynomial over $k$ vanishing at $a_i$, so $a_i$ is integral over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] $A'=k[a_1,\dots,a_n]$ is a finitely generated $k$-module, i.e. $\dim_kA'<\infty$. As a subring of the field $\bar k$, $A'$ is an integral domain (with $1\neq0$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] $A'$ is a field. Thus $k':=A'$ is a subfield with $k\subseteq k'\subseteq\bar k$ and $\dim_kk'<\infty$, $X_{A'}=X_{k'}$, $\pi=p$, and $V'\subseteq X_{k'}$ is a quasi-compact open with $V=p^{-1}(V')$. This is (1).

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 04KU, proof, lines 893--895 ('there exists a finite subextension k'/k'); the source leaves implicit why a finitely generated k-subalgebra of the algebraic extension is a finite field extension, written out here

proof.text: $p\circ\sigma_X=p$ for $\sigma$ fixing $k'$. Let $\iota:k'\hookrightarrow\bar k$ be the inclusion and $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ with $\sigma|_{k'}=\mathrm{id}$, i.e. $\sigma\circ\iota=\iota$. By functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma\circ\iota)=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)$, and by functoriality of base change [def-pc-base-change] (step 1) $p\circ\sigma_X=(\operatorname{Spec}(\iota))_X\circ(\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma))_X=(\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma))_X=(\operatorname{Spec}(\iota))_X=p$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 04KU, proof, lines 895--896 ('Since Gal(k-bar/k') is open ... part (2) is clear'); the invariance under Gal(k-bar/k') is written out here

proof.text: Proof of (2). For $\sigma$ fixing $k'$ pointwise, by step 4 and (1), $\sigma_X^{-1}(V)=\sigma_X^{-1}(p^{-1}(V'))=(p\circ\sigma_X)^{-1}(V')=p^{-1}(V')=V$. Since $\sigma_X$ is a bijection (step 1), $\sigma_X(V)=\sigma_X(\sigma_X^{-1}(V))=V$. (The subgroup of such $\sigma$ is $\operatorname{Gal}(\bar k/k')$, open in $\operatorname{Gal}(\bar k/k)$, which is Stacks' form of (2).)
